title: He Was Cleared on Tuesday. He Was Ruled Out on Wednesday. Hardik Pandya Will Not Play Against Afghanistan.
excerpt: A last-minute leg sprain has ended Pandya's hopes of an ODI return. With Kohli already sidelined, India's World Cup preparation takes another hit.
body:
India's ODI preparations for the 2027 World Cup suffered a fresh blow on Wednesday when Hardik Pandya was ruled out of the three-match series against Afghanistan with a leg sprain. The timing was cruel. Less than twenty-four hours earlier, the Board of Control for Cricket in India had declared him fully fit after a week-long rehabilitation at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

Pandya had been at the CoE since June 2, working through rigorous match simulations that included bowling his full quota of ten overs without discomfort. His fitness data had been signed off by the strength and conditioning staff. The all-rounder appeared certain to return to ODI cricket for the first time since India's Champions Trophy triumph in March 2025.

Then came the sprain. The exact circumstances remain unclear, but BCCI sources confirmed that Pandya sustained a leg injury that makes his participation in the series impossible. No timeline for recovery has been announced, and no replacement has been named.

## Two Pillars, Both Missing

Pandya's withdrawal compounds the absence of Virat Kohli, who was ruled out last week after suffering a hamstring injury during the IPL 2026 final. Kohli had produced a match-winning 75 not out off 42 balls for Royal Challengers Bengaluru against Gujarat Titans on May 31, but the effort came at a cost. The 37-year-old's recovery timeline remains uncertain, with the England tour in July the more pressing concern.

Yashasvi Jaiswal has been named as Kohli's replacement. The left-handed opener scored 171 runs in four ODIs in 2025, including a century, and will likely slot in at number three in Dharamsala on Saturday.

## What Changes for India

Without Pandya and Kohli, India's middle order loses its two most experienced match-winners. The batting lineup for the first ODI at the HPCA Stadium could look significantly different from what most expected.

Shubman Gill leads the side, with Rohit Sharma — who himself passed a fitness test after his own hamstring scare during the IPL — expected to open alongside him. Shreyas Iyer, the newly appointed T20I captain, slots in as vice-captain at number four.

The all-rounder void left by Pandya is the harder one to fill. Nitish Kumar Reddy, who offers pace-bowling and batting depth, is the most likely replacement. Washington Sundar will carry the spin-bowling all-rounder role after his strong showing in the one-off Test, where he took four wickets.

## Debutants Waiting in the Wings

The series also features three uncapped players — Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar, and Harsh Dubey. With Ravindra Jadeja and Axar Patel rested to give younger players exposure ahead of the 2027 World Cup, Dubey — a spin-bowling all-rounder from Vidarbha — could earn an ODI debut as early as the first match.

India head coach Sitanshu Kotak, speaking after the Test victory against Afghanistan, had expressed confidence in Pandya's fitness. That confidence now requires recalibration.

## The Bigger Picture

India sit atop the 2025-27 World Test Championship standings after their innings-and-300-run demolition of Afghanistan in the one-off Test at New Chandigarh. In ODIs, they have won nine of eleven matches in the current World Cup Super League cycle. But the depth of the squad is being tested at exactly the moment when Gill's captaincy tenure needs results.

The first ODI begins on Saturday, June 13 at 1:30 PM IST in Dharamsala. The second moves to Lucknow on June 17, and the series concludes in Chennai on June 20. For Pandya, the focus now shifts to being fit for the England tour, where India play three ODIs and five T20Is starting in July.

The all-rounder will be missed. But for Gill's young squad, this is precisely the kind of adversity that separates a side preparing for a World Cup from one merely planning for it.
